cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Tell Me I Did Enough
cards.instruction: Get someone to reassure you that your effort, choice, or survival was enough.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I only finished one painting for our exhibition. Tell me I've done enough.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll spread mine out. Nobody will notice the gap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. I need to know I've contributed, not that you can hide where I haven't.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yours belongs in the middle. It's the one people will see first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then introduce me as the other painter. No 'despite everything'. I want to hear that I belong here.

mechanism: A judges reassurance offers and directs an unqualified introduction to hear that a limited artistic contribution is enough for belonging.
confusable: D57 demands rank acknowledgment; D100 seeks reassurance of sufficiency despite a perceived shortfall.
comparison: One painting at a joint exhibition differs from staying through a speech with a missing paragraph.
seedUse: Use D100-a gap-hiding offer versus central placement, making B positive solution the basis for requested genuine reassurance.
